newsitem.title: TURKEY: Minister sees S&P raising Turkey rating soon.
newsitem.headline: Minister sees S&P raising Turkey rating soon.

text.p: State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Tuesday he expected the U.S. ratings agency Standard & Poor's to raise Turkey's rating in the near term after lowering it at the end of last week.
"We expect Turkey's credit rating to be justly raised again in the shortest possible time," Soylemez told journalists in parliament.
S&P on Friday cut Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating to "single B" from "single B-plus".

Soylemez said he expected the rating to be raised again in view of privatisations planned from January, measures taken by the government on domestic and foreign debt and new laws being passed by parliament.
He said the government would also seek support from the International Monetary Fund in talks beginning in February.
"We told the IMF: "observe us until the end of January and we will take steps on structural reform'," he said.

He said privatisations, increased foreign currency debt issues and lengthening domestic debt maturities were leading the programme against inflation, currently running at an annual 80 percent in Turkey.
